messages:
Pri (Docs): flagging a quick sync: i'm drafting the release-note + changelog entry for the embed routing refinement. need short 'what changed', migration tip, and aligned SDK snippets. will open a small PR after we lock copy.
Dev (Product): top-level: default routing now biases for latency; deterministic behavior is opt-in. highlight that there's a small, transient token-ordering quirk during cache warm-up. keep the language customer-friendly.
Ava (SDK): i'll prepare JS and Python snippets. question: which enum do we recommend? `route_hint: \"latency\"` and `route_hint: \"deterministic\"` okay?
Rohit (Eng): yes, runtime uses `route_hint`. also note we renamed the model alias from `embed-fast` -> `embed-lowlatency-1`. we put redirects in place but add a callout to encourage updating clients.
Pri (Docs): draft migration line: \"If your application relies on deterministic token order, set `route_hint: \"deterministic\"` while cache alignment completes (may slightly increase latency).\" edit suggestions welcome.
Dev (Product): change 'deterministic token order' -> 'deterministic token ordering' (minor wording). add that no customer data is affected.
Ava (SDK): fine. i'll mirror the exact sentence in SDK README and add a commented note in snippets: `# set route_hint: \"deterministic\" for stable ordering`
Rohit (Eng): adding known-issue phrasing: \"Initial requests after prefix cache cold-start may show minor token-order differences; behavior stabilizes after a few requests.\" KB placeholder: https://kb.redwood.ai/embed-routing-ordering
Pri (Docs): good. i'll add the KB placeholder link and a TOC anchor for Known Issues. also adding a brief 'what changed' bullet: \"Embed routing now defaults to latency-optimized delivery; use `route_hint` to prefer cost or determinism.\"
preview-bot: docs preview available: https://preview.docs.redwood.ai/pr-6120 (build 2) :white_check_mark:
Dev (Product): mobile rendering note: avoid multi-column layouts in release notes; single code block per snippet only. also ensure the curl renders in small screens.
Ava (SDK): will produce single-block snippets. including streaming and non-streaming examples. sample python snippet i'll include below for docs copy: ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=\"$REDWOOD_KEY\")
resp = client.embeddings.create(model=\"embed-lowlatency-1\", route_hint=\"latency\", input=\"hello\")
print(resp.data)
```
Pri (Docs): and a compact curl example for the release note: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"embed-lowlatency-1\",\"route_hint\":\"latency\",\"input\":\"hello\",\"stream\":false}'
```
Rohit (Eng): confirming redirects will respond 301 for `embed-fast` -> `embed-lowlatency-1` for 30 days; we'll confirm timeline in KB before publish.
Pri (Docs): pre-merge checklist: 1) SDK snippets updated and README mirrored (Ava) 2) KB draft with redirect timeline (Rohit) 3) preview review and mobile sanity (Dev) 4) add Known Issues anchor + short blurb (Pri).
Dev (Product): timeline: prefer to publish Thu AM. can we hit that?
Rohit (Eng): KB draft + redirect policy by Wed EOD.
Ava (SDK): snippets + PR by Wed.
Pri (Docs): i'll open the docs PR now and iterate on feedback. tagging reviewers: @Dev (Product) for copy, @Rohit (Eng) for KB confirmation. i'll post once live in #announcements. :tada:
